subject: Re: Horizon Health — DPF evidence, on‑prem options & DPA annex clarifications
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@horizonhealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@horizonhealth.com
Date: 2028-06-12T08:14:00Z
Subject: Initial DPF checklist + on‑prem feasibility questions

Hi Mateo / Marissa,

Thanks for the call this morning. As discussed, Horizon is preparing an internal evidence pack for our legal team and we need clarified answers on a small set of items before we include Redwood in our vendor short‑list. High priority items below — the legal team flagged these for the DPF and the DPA Annex: 

- Transfer mapping: we need a row‑level mapping showing which customer data fields (PHI markers included) may leave EU/UK borders when routed to Redwood-hosted endpoints vs. private on‑prem deployments.
- Legal basis: confirm processor legal basis for processing (Art.6) and whether any margin data is processed under consent or contract.
- DPA Annex edits: we have three proposed language edits to the annex, including a modification to the sub‑processor flowdown clause and a shorter notification window for incidents (48h).
- On‑prem carveouts: can you confirm which components remain customer‑managed in the private (on‑prem/VPC) product and whether any telemetry ever routes back to Redwood control plane?

Can you send a short CSV mapping and point us to any existing DPA Annex template you recommend we use for markups? We are targeting a vendor selection update 06/25 and would appreciate the deliverables by 06/16.

Attachments from our side: sample DPIA extract (redacted) attached in follow‑up.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Legal Operations
Horizon Health

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-13T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial DPF checklist + on‑prem feasibility questions

Alyssa —

Appreciate the clear list. I took point with Marissa and Ben to compile a concise package. Please find the initial deliverables attached:

- redwood_dpf_matrix.csv (rows map common customer fields -> processing locus + transfer jurisdictions + retention basis)
- dpa-annex-template.docx (Redwood recommended baseline with comment bubbles for the three clauses you flagged)
- onprem-deployment-checklist.pdf (what remains in customer control for Private and on‑prem installs; includes KMS/HSM options)

Quick notes (summarized):
1) Transfer mapping: for our hosted API, logs that contain minimal routing metadata may be stored in US regions by default; we include per‑customer region pinning as part of Dedicated/Private contracts to prevent cross‑border persistence. See redwood_dpf_matrix.csv — the PHI flag indicates fields where customers routinely choose region‑pinning.
2) Legal basis: processor operations are under contract (Art.6(1)(b)) for typical SaaS customers; where customers upload data with explicit patient consent, that remains valid but operationally we treat the processing reason as performance of a contract.
3) Incident notification: we generally meet 72h notification for data breaches; 48h is operationally tight for cross‑region forensic work. We can agree to 48h for critical confidentiality incidents with a scoped SLA on forensics support (see comment #7 in dpa‑annex).
4) On‑prem telemetry: in Private on‑prem deployments, telemetry to Redwood control plane is optional and disabled by default; if enabled, the telemetry payload excludes raw customer content and is limited to anonymized runtime metrics.

If you want, Marissa can walk through the DPA Annex comments with your legal team next week.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_dpf_matrix.csv (CSV)]
[Attachment: dpa-annex-template.docx (DOCX)]
[Attachment: onprem-deployment-checklist.pdf (PDF)]

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@horizonhealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@horizonhealth.com
Date: 2028-06-15T09:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial DPF checklist + on‑prem feasibility questions — follow ups

Thanks Mateo — that matrix is very helpful. A few follow‑ups from legal and privacy: 

> On incident notifications: can you confirm the escalation chain and whether Redwood will provide a completed forensic summary within 7 days for incidents scored as "high"?

Also: 
- For private on‑prem installs — will Redwood accept contractual language that explicitly states "no egress of customer content except for signed support bundles"? Our security team wants an explicit guarantee.
- For the DPA Annex: our counsel suggested alternate wording for sub‑processor flowdown that would require prior notice + opt‑out for a 30‑day window. Can we discuss whether Redwood can accept notice + negotiate case‑by‑case for particularly sensitive sub‑processors?

If Marissa/Ben are available, we'd prefer a 30‑minute technical call Wednesday (06/16) or Thursday (06/17) to walk through the matrix and the Annex redlines.

Best,
Alyssa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-18T16:22:00Z
Subject: RE: Initial DPF checklist + on‑prem feasibility questions — scheduling and next steps

Alyssa — thanks for the questions; happy to jump on the call. Proposed plan before the call so we use time efficiently: 

1) Incident process: Ben (cc'd) will draft the forensic SLA language we can commit to for "high" incidents (forensic summary within 7 days + interim status within 48h). We can include a clause for extended investigative support under a paid support addon.

2) No‑egress clause for on‑prem: Redwood will accept "no egress of customer content except for signed support bundles" as contract language for fully air‑gapped on‑prem customers. For Private VPC deployments (managed by Redwood), we propose the signed support bundle process as the operational control. We'll mark the Annex with concrete text options.

3) Sub‑processor flowdown: Redwood's standard approach is notice + 30 days for objections on high‑risk sub‑processors; for most infra sub‑processors (cloud providers, GPU infra) we request case‑by‑case negotiations limited to defined sensitive categories. We'll surface proposed wording in the Annex draft.

Availability: we can do Wednesday 06/16 14:00–14:30 PT or Thursday 06/17 10:00–10:30 PT. Which works best?

Action items: Ben will attach the draft forensic SLA and a short redline excerpt for the Annex prior to the call. Mateo and I will prepare a 2‑slide runbook showing telemetry options and the on‑prem support bundle flow.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: draft_forensic_sla.docx (DOCX)]
